header:
Date: 2027-03-03 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Malik (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Evergreen Head of ML Ops), Liam O'Connor (Evergreen Platform Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Evergreen Data Privacy)
summary: Initial onboarding readiness / runbook handoff for Evergreen Healthworks. Covered deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), data residency and KMS concerns, pilot scope and success metrics, and immediate network checklist. Agreed next steps: send runbook, customer to share traffic profile, schedule Dedicated capacity sizing call.
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone — thanks for hopping on. Quick round of intros, and then we can level set on the onboarding runway.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Hi Ava, Maya here. Liam and Sofia on my side. We're excited to get this rolling, we're under a bit of timeline pressure for a pilot in Q2.
[00:22] Diego Malik: Great, good to hear. I'll capture the action items today.
[00:25] Priya Rao: Hey team, Priya from Redwood SE — I will lead the Dedicated sizing / VPC network steps once we get the traffic samples.
[00:32] Liam O'Connor: Quick note — our infra team prefers VPC private deployment or dedicated capacity behind our VPC peering. We have some PHI-ish data flows so we want to be careful.
[00:44] Sofia Ruiz: And from privacy, we need KMS integration and audit logs for data access, plus retention controls.
[00:52] Ava Chen: Totally expected. Today I want to run through the onboarding runbook, highlight the network checklist, and align on pilot success metrics — latency, cost targets, and quality gates.
[01:06] Maya Patel: Our immediate ask: we'd like to validate both quality against our prompts and cost per 1k tokens. We're comparing hosted vs dedicated pricing.
[01:18] Priya Rao: Ok, if you can share token distribution and peak RPS that helps. For dedicated we typically size by peak concurrent sequences and memory KV cache load. There's also autoscale/burst options.
[01:32] Liam O'Connor: I'll pull the RPS. We expect 60-90 RPS during peak, but avg is much lower — maybe 8-12.
[01:42] Diego Malik: Good. That kind of spiky distribution is exactly where our burst policy can help. We'll propose a reserved baseline and burst to cloud.
[01:52] Maya Patel: What's the typical latency improvement on Dedicated vs Hosted? We have a 200ms P95 target for short prompts.
[02:00] Priya Rao: Short answer: Dedicated plus optimized kernel selection and continuous batching usually reduces tail latency by ~20-40% vs shared hosted profiles, especially for 2-3 token generation calls. But that depends on model and sequence length.
[02:18] Sofia Ruiz: And encryption in transit / at rest? We need KMS/HSM support for keys.
[02:24] Ava Chen: We integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured to use the customer's KMS for model payloads and audit keys. We provide audit logs and token-level tracing in the Console.
[02:36] Maya Patel: Does Redwood retain request payloads in hosted mode?
[02:40] Diego Malik: Hosted default retention is short for debugging but we have options — enterprise packages include no retention and private deployments keep everything off Redwood's control plane. We'll share the data handling doc.
[02:53] Liam O'Connor: Network: we need a checklist for CIDR ranges, peering flow, and egress rules. Also does Redwood support private link / direct connect to our cloud?
[03:04] Priya Rao: Yes — we support Direct Connect and PrivateLink in major clouds; the runbook lists the IP ranges and firewall rules. There can be NAT requirements for outbound callbacks if you call external tools.
[03:17] Maya Patel: Good to know. For the pilot we want to test a constrained prompt set and a production-like traffic replay.
[03:25] Ava Chen: Recommended approach: 1) run a replay of production traffic to our sandbox Dedicated environment, 2) validate latency and quality gates with sample prompts, 3) enable prefix KV caching for hot prefixes. We'll put a step-by-step in the runbook.
[03:41] Liam O'Connor: Prefix caching — we heard about 'KV cache' but our ops folks called it K-V. Any docs on how that affects memory footprint?
[03:48] Priya Rao: Yes, KV cache holds past tokens for chat contexts and increases memory footprint proportional to active sessions and context length. We'll include guidance on cache eviction and sizing heuristics.
[03:59] Maya Patel: On model versions — we want canaries and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency spikes. Is that supported?
[04:07] Priya Rao: Yes, rollouts support canary and automatic fallback rules. You can route by latency SLO or cost tier. We can configure an A/B rollout where 5% goes to the new model and auto-fallback if error rate or latency crosses threshold.
[04:21] Sofia Ruiz: For compliance: SOC2 certs, ISO, and we need a 3rd party pen test report — do you have those?
[04:28] Diego Malik: We will share SOC2 Type II and our latest ISO attestation. For pen test, we have a red team summary; if you need the full report we can arrange an NDA.
[04:38] Maya Patel: Great. On the timeline — our internal stakeholders expect pilot sign-off in 6 weeks. Can Redwood commit to that given lead time for Dedicated capacity?
[04:47] Priya Rao: We can usually stand up a Dedicated pilot in 2-3 weeks if there's available capacity. If you go Private on-prem it'll take longer. We'll do a capacity check after you share the traffic profile.
[04:59] Liam O'Connor: Any special network throughput limits we should plan for? We have big bursts for batch jobs.
[05:06] Priya Rao: For batch we recommend separate scheduling or larger batch window; otherwise it contends with low latency traffic. We'll propose a dedicated worker pool for batch ingestion.
[05:15] Ava Chen: Action item: we'll send the onboarding runbook and the VPC checklist by EOD Monday. Also include the team that handles KMS integration.
[05:25] Maya Patel: On pricing, we will evaluate per-token hosted and committed monthly for Dedicated. Can you include a sample TCO comparison for our traffic profile?
[05:33] Diego Malik: Yes — once you send the token distribution and peak RPS, Priya and I will build a TCO spreadsheet and two scenarios (hosted vs dedicated).
[05:44] Speaker 1: (inaudible) — small note on logging retention windows, we need 12 months for certain audit trails.
[05:51] Sofia Ruiz: Correct, retention windows are critical. Do you support export to our SIEM?
[05:56] Priya Rao: We have log shipping integrations (S3, Splunk, Datadog) and can retain logs per contract. We'll add SIEM export steps in the runbook.
[06:06] Liam O'Connor: Regarding SSO, we use Okta and SAMl, does Redwood support group-based RBAC mapping?
[06:13] Ava Chen: Yes, SAML SSO with group mapping, and fine-grained RBAC through the Console. We'll include config steps for Okta.
[06:23] Maya Patel: For the pilot, success criteria: 1) P95 latency under 220ms on short prompts, 2) cost per 1k tokens within X% of our threshold (we'll define), 3) no privacy violations in replay tests.
[06:35] Diego Malik: Noted. We'll also add a quality monitoring baseline using your prompt set and Redwood Optimize watch rules for regressions.
[06:45] Maya Patel: Who will be our day-to-day CSM?
[06:48] Diego Malik: That's me, Diego — I'll be your CSM. Priya will handle the technical plan, and Ava will be your go-to for commercial / account items.
[06:56] Maya Patel: Perfect. Any red flags from Redwood that could delay go-live?
[06:59] Priya Rao: Biggest potential delays: Dedicated capacity availability and network approvals on your side (firewall rules, peering). Also KMS provisioning needs coordination with your security team.
[07:13] Liam O'Connor: We'll prioritize the network ticket and loop in security for KMS.
[07:17] Ava Chen: Ok recap: Redwood sends runbook + VPC checklist; customer provides token distribution and peak RPS; schedule Dedicated sizing call for week of 3/14; Redwood to deliver TCO comparison and SOC2 docs.
[07:31] Maya Patel: That works. One small ask — can you include a one-page 'rollback and incident playbook' for the pilot?
[07:36] Diego Malik: Yes, we'll include a one-page incident and rollback playbook describing automatic fallback, alert routing, and escalation contacts.
[07:44] Sofia Ruiz: Also, include the data deletion procedures and proof points for retention compliance.
[07:49] Ava Chen: We'll add data deletion steps and certificated timelines.
[07:54] Priya Rao: I'll follow up on memory footprints for KV cache and draft a sample autoscale policy.
[07:59] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — that's a useful session. We'll aim to have the RPS and token spreadsheet by Wednesday.
[08:05] Ava Chen: Awesome, thanks all. We'll send the runbook and schedule the Dedicated sizing session once we have the data.
[08:11] Liam O'Connor: Thanks.
[08:12] Meeting ended.
